T01.name: Source-citation omission
T01.definition: Leaving out data-source or other provenance information the audience would need in order to assess the data; treated as an omission because professional producers are assumed to know provenance matters.

T02.name: Ambiguous variable definition
T02.definition: Presenting variables whose definitions or membership criteria are left unclear, so users cannot know exactly what is measured and may default to whichever reading their own viewing codes support.

T03.name: Knowledge assumption
T03.definition: Communicating in a way that only makes sense if users supply unstated propositions or intermediate reasoning steps themselves.

T04.name: Thresholding
T04.definition: Excluding values above or below chosen cut points. Visual instance: setting the axis range around the values most important to the intended comparison so that relevant higher/lower values are not shown.

T05.name: Exceptional-case omission
T05.definition: Excluding outliers or complicating cases from the representation in order to simplify the phenomenon.

T06.name: User-transferred filtering
T06.definition: Shifting the information-loss choice onto the end-user via filtering capabilities (e.g. search bars), so the user selects the subset that is shown.

T07.name: Variable selection
T07.definition: Choosing which variables from a larger data set to visualize; the chosen subset stands in for the whole.

T08.name: Averaging
T08.definition: Substituting a simpler central representation for a wider range of values.

T09.name: Summaries
T09.definition: Substituting summary text or summary graphics for the fuller underlying data.

T10.name: Aggregation / binning
T10.definition: Grouping values into categories, bins or aggregates so that an intended effect becomes more apparent; may be applied inconsistently across series.

T11.name: Source citation
T11.definition: Naming or hyperlinking the origin of the data.

T12.name: Additional references
T12.definition: Supplying further reading or supporting references beyond the primary data source.

T13.name: Methodology citation
T13.definition: Explaining the methodological choices behind the data collection or the graphic.

T14.name: Relevant facts
T14.definition: Supplying contextual facts that situate or qualify the data.

T15.name: Exception annotation
T15.definition: Explicitly flagging known exceptions, errata or corrections to the data or graphic.

T16.name: Visual uncertainty
T16.definition: Encoding uncertainty visually, e.g. error bars or confidence envelopes.

T17.name: Inferential limits
T17.definition: Textual statements of confidence intervals, margins of error or other inferential limits.

T18.name: Forecast annotation
T18.definition: Explicitly labelling the point at which data become extrapolated, predicted or forecast.

T19.name: Expression of doubt
T19.definition: Hedging statements about the strength of potential conclusions.

T20.name: Author bio
T20.definition: Providing biographical information about the designer beyond a simple credit line.

T21.name: Personal anecdote
T21.definition: The designer disclosing personal stories or perspective within the presentation.

T22.name: Perceptual noise
T22.definition: Introducing noise at a perceptual level, e.g. a decorative 3D effect that degrades value judgement.

T23.name: Sizing distortion
T23.definition: Sizing that violates discriminability limits: elements too small for judgement, oversizing that overwhelms the presentation, or obscuring a value true position on an axis.

T24.name: Poor channel mapping
T24.definition: Failing (often unintentionally) to map important information to the most accurately judged visual channels, per graphical-perception rankings.

T25.name: False cause-effect
T25.definition: Design choices that imply causal relationships the data do not support.

T26.name: Double axis
T26.definition: Using constructions that experts note are difficult to decode even when properly used, e.g. dual axes.

T27.name: Spatial metaphor
T27.definition: Layout exploiting embodied conventions such as left = past / right = future, or up = more/better, down = less/bad; interpreted automatically.

T28.name: Typographic mapping
T28.definition: Pairing visualized patterns to categories via type treatment.

T29.name: Color mapping
T29.definition: Colors carrying categorical or cultural meaning, e.g. party colors applied to election statistics.

T30.name: Visual noise
T30.definition: Deliberately confusing visuals standing in for the confusion of the subject matter; can simultaneously obscure.

T31.name: Visual contrast
T31.definition: Juxtaposing oppositional pieces of information visually so comparison itself carries the message.

T32.name: Variable splice
T32.definition: Including variables not obviously associated with the target variables, implying that comparing them will yield further insight.

T33.name: Visual grouping
T33.definition: Visually grouping marks to assert category or priority structure.

T34.name: Typographic classification
T34.definition: Consistent font sizes/styles used to classify information within the visualization.

T35.name: Significance equation
T35.definition: Legend-like devices that highlight certain values as significant, imposing clusters of priority or importance.

T36.name: Redundancy
T36.definition: Repeating identical labels, or disaggregating values with little variance, to emphasize (or to create visual noise); violates the one-to-one data-visual mapping expected in strict InfoVis taxonomies.

T37.name: Typographic emphasis
T37.definition: Font emphasis whose meaning derives from long-standing typographic convention.

T38.name: Rhetorical question
T38.definition: A question posed to engage the user by direct address while implying its own (often obvious) answer; frequently in titles.

T39.name: Scare quotes
T39.definition: Quotation marks that distance or ironize a term, cueing an implied alternative meaning.

T40.name: Understatement
T40.definition: Understating a point so that the discrepancy itself communicates.

T41.name: Analogy
T41.definition: Comparing two entities to give insight into the lesser-known of the two.

T42.name: Metaphor
T42.definition: Equating two ideas by labelling or directly asserting that one is the other.

T43.name: Parallelism
T43.definition: Expressing two linguistic statements or visual features so they read as equal in importance.

T44.name: Simile
T44.definition: Explicit like/as comparison used for effect and emphasis of a similarity relationship.

T45.name: Double entendre
T45.definition: A single expression or visual form carrying two meanings via linguistic or visual similarity alone.

T46.name: Apostrophe
T46.definition: Directly addressing the end-user in titles and annotations, including via rhetorical questions and suggested goals.

T47.name: Exploratory functions
T47.definition: Offering sorting/filtering and similar functions as a personal appeal to the individual user.

T48.name: Citizen framing
T48.definition: Phrasing or imagery framed from an ordinary individual viewpoint (people icons, buy-insurance wording), cueing a viewing code that privileges the individual.

T49.name: Default view
T49.definition: The initial visual configuration anchors interpretation to whatever it shows first.

T50.name: Fixed comparison
T50.definition: Pre-loading reference values by default so users contrast other values against them; risky because users lack shared norms for judging visual significance.

T51.name: Spatial ordering
T51.definition: Ordering content to exploit reading and scanning conventions so some information is prioritized.

T52.name: Animation
T52.definition: Using time to suggest a story; pausing or ending on particular views prioritizes them through a climactic effect.

T53.name: Search suggestion
T53.definition: Suggested queries prompting the user to examine particular parts of the data rather than explore freely.

T54.name: Goal suggestion
T54.definition: Prompts or instructions to look for particular patterns.

T55.name: Search bar
T55.definition: Letting users constrain the depiction to personally relevant subsets; effective because personalization increases the message salience.

T56.name: Menuing
T56.definition: Menu options (and their ordering) steering users toward comparisons and views the designers found most interesting while exploring the data.
